vision._note: gopiv is a BENCH TEST RIG (one motor, no wheels, never on the playfield); no physical AprilTag is mounted. robot_tag_id inherited from the template for schema completeness only.
vision._tag_id_note: 2026-08-27, stakeholder: this robot physically carries tag 54. Corrected from 100. The 100 in this file did not match the marker actually mounted on the robot -- a stale config value, not a renumbering. Anything that resolved gopiv by tag 100 (an aprilcam mobile-tag registration in particular) must be re-registered against 54, or it will report the wrong robot's centre.

geometry._geometry_note: 2026-08-27, camera-truthed on the main playfield, gopiv on firmware 0.20260827.2. trackwidth 114.8 mm is the STAKEHOLDER'S CALIPER measurement and is never corrected to make a turn land -- motion_engine.h is explicit that it is the one independently verifiable number in the geometry, and that all rotational scrub belongs in rotational_slip, since effectiveTrackWidth() = trackWidth / rotationalSlip. Was 128, which matched nothing. rotational_slip 0.9633 = 114.8 / 119.2, where 119.2 mm is the camera-measured EFFECTIVE track. METHOD, and why the first two attempts were wrong: effective track was derived from the SLOPE of a pivot sweep (4 sizes x 3 reps x both directions, 40/70/100/130 mm per wheel), fitting d_theta = 0.9616 deg/mm * d + 10.19 deg. Deriving it from any SINGLE pivot size instead gives a different answer every time -- 90 mm/wheel implied 107.4 mm and 47 mm/wheel implied 88.1 mm -- because a +10.2 deg FIXED per-pivot term (overshoot/coast, not scrub) is otherwise absorbed into the scale. That constant must NOT be folded into rotational_slip: slip is a scale, and baking the offset into it fits one pivot size and mis-turns every other. CLAUDE.md warns about exactly this shape -- a constant per-pivot offset does not cancel the way a scale error does. The 10.2 deg term is UNEXPLAINED and uncorrected; rotation_gain_*/rotation_offset_* below are where it would belong, but see the next note. INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION: the pxt-nezha-diffdrive firmware carries its own baked defaults, motion_engine.h trackWidth_ = 114.2f and rotationalSlip_ = 0.952f, i.e. an effective track of 119.96 mm. The camera measurement here is 119.2 mm -- 0.6% apart, arrived at with no knowledge of those constants.
geometry._not_read_by_pxt_firmware_note: 2026-08-27: NOTHING in this geometry block reaches the pxt-nezha-diffdrive firmware. tools/make_deploy.py injects only the radio channel, kProfile, kVersion and the boot banner; test.ts never calls _setGeometry(); and grep finds no reader for rotation_gain_* or rotation_offset_* anywhere in that repo's src/. The robot runs motion_engine.h's baked trackWidth_/rotationalSlip_ instead. So editing this file changes host-side tooling and nothing on the robot. rotational_slip IS reachable at runtime -- it is a wire-settable config field (SET rotational_slip) -- but that is RAM-only and does not survive a reset. Changing what the robot ships with means editing motion_engine.h and reflashing.

wheel_control._stall_note: 2026-08-09: added so this robot can be BUILT at all -- gen_boot_config.py requires all three (config-as-truth, sprint 114) and they were added to tovez.json only, which left gopiv and togov unbuildable. Held at 0, which is the documented INERT state, not a guess: tovez.json's own _stall_note says 'the whole detector is inert on any robot whose JSON leaves stall_window at 0'. gopiv has no drive characterization of its own, and tovez's numbers (15.0 / 40.0 / 500.0) are DESIGN CHOICES derived from tovez's own measured v_min, deadband and planner.a_max -- none of which have been measured here -- so borrowing them would be a fabricated calibration, not a default. Same posture togov.json takes for its uncharacterized wheel_control group. Replace with gopiv's own numbers before relying on stall detection on this robot. NOTE: togov.json still has this gap and is still unbuildable.

planner._timing_note: control_period/actuation_delay are '= App::RobotLoop::kCycle' by construction; both moved 50.0 -> 32.0 with kCycle on 2026-08-07. See data/robots/tovez.json's own planner._timing_note for the measurements and the full history.

navigator._navigator_note: 135-004: seeded from Motion::NavigatorLimits' own compile-time defaults (src/firm/motion/navigator/arc_solver.h) -- same pattern as tovez.json's own navigator block (see that file's note for the full rationale). yaw_sign=1.0 (identity, unmeasured) pending this robot's own bench pass -- tovez.json's -1.0 is a tovez-specific measured fact (src/tests/bench/goto_otos.py's own YAW_SIGN), not assumed to transfer to a different drivetrain without its own measurement.

encoders._note: the rig has ONE physical motor; the firmware's differential config still models two channels.

_provenance_note: 2026-08-05: reconstructed FROM THE RUNNING DEVICE via protocol v5 GetConfig read-back of all eight groups (rogo repl 'get <group>' against gopiv, firmware 0.20260804.6, every group BAKED) -- the gopiv.json that built 0.20260804.6 was not in this repo. All wire-group values are the device's own, float32 round-trip artifacts rounded back (0.7048599720001221 -> 0.70486 etc.). Non-wire sections (identity/vision/wheels/encoders/gripper/peripherals) are template-shaped from tovez.json and marked where they are placeholders. Radio channel: the firmware pins channel 0 in main.cpp (no config field, no wire verb); the 2026-08-05 bench flash carries a main.cpp literal radio.begin(1) NOT committed anywhere -- adding a proper radio-channel config field is the durable fix.
